documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
65 yo woman transferring care. Retired admin assistant, lives with her husband. Brought every bottle in a shopping bag, which helped.

HPI: Diabetes for about 15 years, never well controlled per her report; on metformin and glyburide, checks sugars maybe twice a week, fasting usually 150s-190s. No lows she knows of. HTN on three agents. Kidney function has been drifting down for a couple of years and she was told stage 3. RA since her mid-50s, hands mostly, on weekly methotrexate and daily prednisone 10 mg from her rheumatologist, whose office is closing to new referrals from her old group so she needs a new one. COPD: never smoked, but has had a bad chest for years; dyspnea on one flight of stairs, uses rescue inhaler a few times a week. Reflux controlled on omeprazole.

PMH: T2DM, HTN, CKD 3b, RA, COPD (severe per prior PFTs), GERD.
PSH: TAH at 52 for fibroids.
Meds: reconciled from bottles, see list. Takes calcium and D because of the prednisone.
Allergies: none to drugs.
FHx: Mother with T2DM and osteoporosis. Father with HTN and COPD. Maternal aunt broke a hip from osteoporosis.
SHx: Never smoker. Wine 1-2 glasses a week. No drugs.

ROS: Chronic exertional dyspnea, morning stiffness in hands ~30 min. Otherwise negative.

Exam: Vitals as charted. Pleasant, in no distress. Lungs with diminished breath sounds at both bases, prolonged expiration, no wheeze today. Heart regular, no murmur. Abdomen soft. Hands with mild MCP swelling bilaterally, no warmth. No leg edema. Feet: skin intact, monofilament sensation intact, DP pulses 2+.

A/P:
1. T2DM, poorly controlled - A1c today. Will revisit regimen once labs back; glyburide in her kidney range is not ideal, noted for next visit.
2. HTN - 138/82, near goal on three drugs, continue.
3. CKD 3b - BMP and urine albumin today; referral to nephrology since she has none locally.
4. RA - continues MTX/prednisone; referral to rheumatology for ongoing management and MTX monitoring.
5. COPD - severe by history, continue ICS/LABA and albuterol. Will request old PFTs.
6. GERD - stable.
7. HM - records request for vaccines, colonoscopy, mammogram. HCV screen today. Flu/pneumonia vaccines at a nurse visit next month.

Return 3 months.

Outpatient Nephrology Consultation
Date of service: 10/30/2019
Reason: CKD 3b, referred by her primary care physician.

Thank you for sending Ms. Fischer, a 65 year old woman with long-standing type 2 diabetes, hypertension, RA on methotrexate and prednisone, and severe COPD. Creatinine has risen from about 1.2 to 1.35 over two years. Urine albumin to creatinine ratio 210 mg/g. No hematuria. No NSAID use. BP 136/80 here.

Impression: CKD stage 3b, most consistent with diabetic and hypertensive kidney disease, moderately increased albuminuria.

Recommendations: Continue lisinopril. Avoid NSAIDs and IV contrast where possible. I would watch metformin dosing as filtration falls. Methotrexate is renally cleared; rheumatology aware. We will see her yearly with labs beforehand.

Meds reviewed: metformin, glyburide, lisinopril, amlodipine, HCTZ, omeprazole, prednisone, methotrexate, fluticasone-salmeterol, albuterol, aspirin, calcium, vitamin D3.
Allergies: NKDA.

ENDOCRINOLOGY CONSULT
Visit date: 02/18/2021
Referring: primary care

Reason for referral: persistent fatigue, generalized weakness and bone pain that has not improved on osteoporosis therapy.

History: 67-year-old woman with poorly controlled type 2 diabetes and hypertension of long standing, with steadily falling kidney function over many years, now CKD 3b and followed by nephrology. Osteoporosis diagnosed last spring (DXA lumbar spine T -2.8), on alendronate since May 2020. Reports months of tiredness, weakness and aching bones. RA and severe COPD on daily prednisone 10 mg and weekly methotrexate.

Medications (per patient list): metformin 1000 BID, glyburide 5, lisinopril 20, amlodipine 5, HCTZ 12.5, omeprazole 20, prednisone 10, methotrexate 15/wk, fluticasone-salmeterol, albuterol PRN, aspirin 81, alendronate 70/wk, calcium carbonate 600 TID, cholecalciferol 2000 IU.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family: mother T2DM and osteoporosis; father HTN and COPD; maternal aunt hip fracture.
Social: never smoker, wine occasionally, retired administrative assistant.

Exam: Mild edema of both lower legs. Pallor. No thyroid enlargement. Proximal strength mildly reduced. Spine non-tender.

Data: Hemoglobin 10.8, normocytic (PCP labs 1/12). Today: creatinine 1.6, calcium 9.3, phosphorus 4.6, intact PTH 186 pg/mL. 25-OH vitamin D 34 in January. DXA 4/2020 reduced bone density as above.

Assessment:
1. Hyperparathyroidism with normal calcium and raised PTH in the setting of CKD 3b - secondary hyperparathyroidism of renal origin. I spoke with her nephrologist, who reads the labs the same way.
2. Normocytic anemia, iron replete - anemia of CKD; nephrology will follow.
3. Osteoporosis on alendronate; bone pain likely reflects mineral-bone disease of CKD in part.

Plan: No medication change. Continue vitamin D3 2000 IU and calcium. Nephrology to trend PTH and phosphorus. Return to endocrinology in one year.

Endocrinology clinic

Steroid myopathy explains the proximal weakness, and steroids are worsening her glucose control, blood pressure and bone loss. Recommendations: The prednisone dose is the central issue. Would ask rheumatology to look at steroid-sparing options for her RA; I recognize her lung disease complicates any taper. Do not stop prednisone abruptly - adrenal suppression is expected. Continue alendronate, calcium and D. Return in one year.

ED PHYSICIAN NOTE
Arrival 02/24/2025 15:20

Chief complaint: painful blistering rash on the left side x 3 days.

HPI: 71-year-old woman on methotrexate and chronic prednisone for RA, with vulvar SCC treated in 2023, presents with a rash that started as a patch of red bumps on the left side of her trunk and turned into fluid-filled blisters, all in one strip wrapping toward her back. Burning pain. No fever. No recent illness. Says she has been very stressed looking after her husband, who has been unwell.

PMH: T2DM, HTN (on HCTZ among others), CKD 3b, osteoporosis with wrist fracture 2024, severe COPD, GERD, secondary hyperparathyroidism.

Labs: HIV antibody negative. Fasting glucose 148. CBC unremarkable for her (white count and platelets normal, hemoglobin at her usual CKD level). ESR 20 mm/hr (normal <20).

documents.title: ICU and hospital discharge summary
documents.author: critical care
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY - regional medical center
Admitted 02/25/2026 (via ED to ICU)  Discharged 03/17/2026

Diagnoses: septic shock, source not identified; acute kidney failure due to diffuse renal cortical necrosis (biopsy-proven), not recovered - now dialysis dependent.

Presentation: 72-year-old woman with severe COPD, CKD 3b (baseline creatinine about 1.7), poorly controlled T2DM, RA on methotrexate and prednisone 10 mg daily. Two days of high fevers and shaking chills at home, then her husband found her confused. On arrival: T 39.4, BP 78/42, HR 124, RR 26, SpO2 92% on room air. Cool extremities, slow capillary refill, dry mouth. Creatinine 3.9, BUN 68, lactate 5.2, WBC 19.6.

Hospital course:
- Shock: IV fluid resuscitation, norepinephrine for 3 days, broad-spectrum antibiotics (vancomycin and piperacillin-tazobactam), stress-dose hydrocortisone given chronic prednisone. Blood and urine cultures without growth; chest film without consolidation; no source identified. Antibiotics completed. Mental status back to baseline by day 2.
- Kidneys: urine output remained low despite resuscitation and creatinine kept climbing; anuric by day 4. Ultrasound with normal-sized kidneys, no obstruction. Hemodialysis started day 5 through a temporary femoral catheter. Renal biopsy 3/3: diffuse cortical necrosis. No return of urine output over the following two weeks. Tunneled right internal jugular dialysis catheter placed 3/10. Accepted to an outpatient in-center unit, three treatments a week.
- Steroids: hydrocortisone tapered back to prednisone 10 mg daily.
- Diabetes: oral agents stopped; basal insulin started.
- Lungs: no intubation this admission; oxygen weaned to room air.

Discharge medication changes:
STOPPED: metformin, glyburide, lisinopril, hydrochlorothiazide, methotrexate, alendronate.
STARTED: insulin glargine 8 units at bedtime.
CONTINUED: prednisone 10 mg daily, amlodipine 5 mg daily, omeprazole 20 mg, aspirin 81 mg, fluticasone-salmeterol, albuterol as needed, calcium carbonate with meals, cholecalciferol.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.

Follow-up: PCP within 1 week; nephrology at the dialysis unit; rheumatology regarding RA treatment off methotrexate.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM visit. RN contact 3/18. Discharge summary received 3/19 and reviewed in full.

Three-week ICU and hospital stay for septic shock without a source found, complicated by kidney failure - biopsy showed diffuse cortical necrosis and she never made urine again. Now on in-center hemodialysis three times a week via a right chest tunneled catheter. Came straight from a dialysis morning; husband drove.

She is exhausted and weak, walking with a cane in the house for now. Eating small amounts. No fever. Breathing at baseline. Mind clear. Fingersticks 140s-230s on glargine 8 units.

Med reconciliation: list updated to the discharge changes - metformin, glyburide, lisinopril, HCTZ, methotrexate and alendronate off; glargine 8 units at bedtime on. She has the pen and was taught at discharge; technique reviewed. Prednisone 10, amlodipine 5, omeprazole, aspirin, inhalers, calcium, D3 continue.

Exam: Vitals as charted - weight down several kilos. Thin, tired. Catheter site right upper chest clean, dressing intact. Lungs distant, no crackles. Heart regular. No edema.

A/P:
1. ESRD on hemodialysis after diffuse cortical necrosis - nephrology/dialysis unit managing; I'll get their notes. CKD 3b closed out, ESRD added.
2. Septic shock - resolved.
3. T2DM - glargine 8 units; she will keep a log and the RN will call Thursday. A1c today knowing it is less reliable with dialysis and anemia.
4. RA - methotrexate off; rheumatology appointment requested; prednisone continues, do not stop.
5. Deconditioning - home safety reviewed; she declines home PT, will walk at home.
RTC 6-8 weeks.

documents.title: Glucose check
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called for sugar log as planned. Fasting 138, 162, 151; one bedtime reading of 244 after a large supper. No lows, no symptoms of lows. Pen technique fine. A1c from Tuesday 8.3 - PCP aware, no dose change for now. Reminded her to bring the log to dialysis too. Next PCP visit May 12.

Nephrology monthly dialysis note, 04/14/2026.

ESRD after biopsy-proven diffuse cortical necrosis with septic shock in late February; anuric. In-center hemodialysis three times weekly via right IJ tunneled catheter, tolerating treatments; dry weight being set. Fistula planning referral placed by our unit.

Monthly labs: pre-dialysis creatinine 6.4, potassium 4.8, hemoglobin 9.6. Phosphorus and PTH being followed at the unit with dietary counseling; calcium carbonate continues with meals.

Meds reviewed against discharge list; no changes from our side. Alendronate and methotrexate remain off. Insulin per PCP.

Sugars: fasting mostly 130s-160s on glargine 8 units, no lows. Nephrology April note reviewed (Hb 9.6, K 4.8). Rheum: MTX stays off, prednisone continues.

Exam: vitals as charted. Catheter site clean. Lungs distant. Regular rhythm. No edema.

A/P: ESRD on HD - per nephrology. T2DM - continue glargine 8 units; A1c at next visit. RA - stable on prednisone alone for now. COPD stable. RTC July.

documents.author: PCP

S: Four months into hemodialysis. Doing her own errands again on non-dialysis days. Sugars fasting 120s-150s, no hypoglycemia. Breathing fine in the heat with the controller. Joints ok on prednisone. Gyn onc in June: no evidence of disease. Husband's health about the same.

Meds reviewed: glargine 8 units qhs, prednisone 10, amlodipine 5, omeprazole 20, aspirin 81, fluticasone-salmeterol, albuterol prn, calcium carbonate, D3.

O: vitals as charted. Catheter site clean. Lungs distant without wheeze. Heart regular. No edema. Feet: intact skin, sensation normal to monofilament, pulses present.

A/P: T2DM on basal insulin - A1c today; no change unless above 8. ESRD on HD - nephrology. RA, COPD stable. Flu and COVID vaccines in the fall; dialysis unit may give flu, she will let us know. RTC October.
